checkout_rails: No public in-site checkout rails observed on Doji site or App Store; public surfaces show app download and extension-based flow but no runnable web checkout or merchant-facing cart/checkout UI.
value.expectation_copy: "Upload a few photos, create your photorealistic AI likeness and try on real fashion products effortlessly."  and "Try on clothes with your likeness" appear in Doji's marketing/App Store materials. These lines state a real-fashion try-on promise but do not guarantee SKU-level fidelity or fit accuracy in public outputs.
value.gap_vs_onpoint: Doji input flow exhibits named garment inputs and a Try On action, plus a Safari extension promise, but public-facing output does not reveal SKU-level fidelity, real-time stock, local-pay rails, or an agent/API surface. There is no observable supply-graph of local curators, no public inventory/price/fulfillment data, and no public agent/OpenAPI surface. Doji’s mobile-first, iPhone-only path and invite-only extension imply limited reach and transactional surface, which leaves a gap relative to OnPoint’s model of fit-aware, stock-specific, locally-payable, agent-addressable supply graph.
value.pricing_tiers: Free to download on App Store; no public paid tier surfaced during this review; iOS 18+ required; no in-app purchases observed in the public view.
value.product: Doji AI-powered virtual try-on platform (US market) with named garment inputs and an AI-likeness-based output; marketing emphasizes extension for browser-based try-on, and an iPhone-only app.

value.value_proposition: Create your AI likeness, explore a personalized feed of looks, try on real fashion items through named product inputs, and save/sharable looks.
value.what_onpoint_should_copy: OnPoint should leverage a concise emotional hook akin to Doji's: 'See it in your world. Buy it from a real local curator.' Build a product-input flow with concrete item cards (SKU, variant, stock provenance) and a local, curator-driven payment/fulfillment path (e.g., WhatsApp + M-Pesa, local currency, etc.). Emphasize curators and cultural supply (e.g., Ankara, Kente, Adire, Bogolan, Shweshwe) with provenance and locality. Distinguish clearly between likeness-based outputs and exact garment fidelity, and provide a visible supply-graph behind the UI showing stock, origin, and payment options to support trust and conversion.
